questions.cardText:
[Geology] What causes the vibrant colors of hot springs in Yellowstone National Park?
A. Microbes
B. Mineral deposits
C. Sunlight reflection on the changing density of water at different temperature
Answer: A. The striking colors of the hot springs are due to the presence of algae, bacteria, and archaea that thrive in hot water (as hot as 165 °F or about 73 °C). Their pigments create the vivid blues, greens, and yellows seen in the pool.
questions.de: Was verleiht Thermalquellen im Yellowstone wie der Grand Prismatic Spring ihre leuchtenden Farbringe?
questions.en: What gives Yellowstone hot springs such as the Grand Prismatic Spring their vivid rings of colour?
questions.answerDe: Mikrobenmatten aus wärmeliebenden Bakterien und Archaeen
questions.answerEn: Microbial mats of heat-loving bacteria and archaea

timeline.labelEn: The Hayden Geological Survey sees the Grand Prismatic Spring and names it for its colours
timeline.labelDe: Die Hayden-Expedition sichtet die Grand Prismatic Spring und benennt sie nach ihren Farben

questions.notes: Card slightly off: the colourful edges are microbial mats of thermophilic bacteria and archaea (green to red, by chlorophyll/carotenoid ratio); the deep blue centre is the water itself, too hot for mats, not microbial pigment. 'Algae' is loose wording for cyanobacteria.

questions.cardText:
[Engineering and Inventions] What was the first product to have a barcode?
A. A pack of gum
B. A bottle of soda
C. A book
Answer: A.
questions.de: Welches Produkt wurde 1974 in Troy (Ohio) als erstes überhaupt an einer Supermarktkasse per UPC-Strichcode gescannt?
questions.en: What was the first product ever scanned by a UPC barcode at a supermarket checkout, in Troy, Ohio, in 1974?
questions.answerDe: Eine Packung Wrigley's Juicy Fruit Kaugummi
questions.answerEn: A pack of Wrigley's Juicy Fruit chewing gum

timeline.labelEn: A pack of Juicy Fruit gum becomes the first UPC-scanned item, at a Marsh supermarket in Troy, Ohio
timeline.labelDe: Eine Packung Juicy-Fruit-Kaugummi wird in einem Marsh-Supermarkt in Troy, Ohio, als erster Artikel per UPC gescannt

questions.notes: Card imprecise: the gum was the first item scanned with a UPC at a checkout, not the first product to carry a barcode (barcodes e.g. on railway cars predate it).
